thread:
maya-support: Heads up — getting a handful of reports that hourly usage metrics are delayed ~3-4h in the console for some tenants (acme, brightline). Not seeing new rollup rows for hour buckets after 01:00 UTC. Anyone on call or seen alerts?

ingest-bot: ALERT: consumer_lag > 450k on topic `rollups.hourly.v2` (consumer group: analytics-rollup-consumers). First seen: 2026-03-07T01:12:00Z.

ben-eng: I can join. Quick check: airflow shows the rollup DAG ran at 01:00 but the task `write_rollups` retried a few times. Logs show KV write timeouts to rollup-db. Pasting tail: 
```
2026-03-07T01:05:02Z ERROR write_rollups tenant=acme batch=120 err=pgx: canceling statement due to statement timeout
2026-03-07T01:05:02Z WARN  retrying batch tenant=acme attempt=2
```

liam-sre: I'm seeing a sustained Kafka partition skew on `rollups.hourly.v2`. One partition has ~400k messages and is owned by a single consumer instance (consumer-3). Other partitions are nearly empty. Consumer group rebalance spam in the logs: `KafkaError: fetch throttled`.

anna-data: That partition contains most of acme and brightline keys — looks like our partitioner has been picking `{tenant_id % N}` but N changed after an N->N+2 cluster resize last night and we didn't rebalance keys.

maya-support: So root cause candidate = partition skew after cluster resize + consumer throttling causing backlog -> write timeouts -> retries -> airflow task backpressure. Sounds plausible. What's safe to run to unblock dashboards quickly?

ben-eng: Short-term plan: (1) temporarily scale analytics-rollup-consumers from 3 -> 6 to spread consumption, (2) trigger targeted backfill for affected hour ranges for specific tenants (avoid full backfill), (3) watch for double-writes in rollup-db. I can do the scale and job kickoff.

liam-sre: I'm going to reassign the hot partition across brokers to reduce IO pressure. Also increasing kafka `fetch.max.bytes` and lowering `consumer.max.poll.interval.ms` may help immediate throttling. Doing broker reassign now.

ben-eng: Scaling consumers: `kubectl scale deployment analytics-rollup-consumers --replicas=6 -n analytics-prod` — kicked.

ben-eng: Starting targeted backfill for acme and brightline for hours 01:00-05:00 UTC: `python tools/backfill_rollups.py --tenants acme,brightline --from 2026-03-07T01:00Z --to 2026-03-07T05:00Z --dry-run=false`

anna-data: For safety, the backfill job writes to a staging table `rollups_hourly_staging` and then `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (tenant_id,hour) DO UPDATE SET ...` — should be idempotent but monitor counters for duplicates.

ingest-bot: INFO: consumer_lag decreased to 120k on `rollups.hourly.v2` after scaling.

ben-eng: Backfill started, ETA ~18m for the tenant set. Watching rollup-db 95th write latency. Queries to check progress: `SELECT hour, count(*) FROM rollups_hourly_staging WHERE tenant_id in ('acme','brightline') GROUP BY hour;`

liam-sre: Broker reassign finished. The hot partition is now spread across brokers, I also bumped `replica.fetch.max.bytes` temporarily.

maya-support: Any sign the console is picking up the new rows?

ben-eng: Getting rows in staging. Pushing staging -> main for hours up to 04:00. Ran: `BEGIN; INSERT ... ON CONFLICT ...; COMMIT;` — no errors.

ingest-bot: ALERT RESOLVED: consumer_lag < 5k.

anna-data: Quick postmortem notes while fresh: root cause = partitioner key distribution mismatch after broker/partition count change => tenant key hot-shard. Secondary impact = consumer throttling and rollup-db write timeouts causing airflow retries and delayed hourly availability.

ben-eng: Backfill completed for acme, brightline. Console shows updated metrics up to 05:00 UTC. Marking this as mitigated. Follow-ups: (1) add a periodic rebalance job after partition count changes, (2) add alert for tenant-partition-skew (one partition > 20x median messages), (3) harden rollup write timeouts and exponential backoff.

liam-sre: Added a temporary k8s autoscaler rule to allow scaling to 8 consumers if lag > 200k for >10m. We'll revisit permanent setting.

maya-support: Thanks all — customers notified via support ticket that dashboards will be up-to-date and that we're following up with infra changes. :thumbsup:

anna-data: I'll open a follow-up ticket in PCM to implement deterministic hashing change (tenant_id -> consistent_hash % partitions) and schedule a controlled rebalance next maintenance window.

ben-eng: Leaving a note in runbook under `rollups/partition-skew` with commands we used and queries to detect. Closing thread after I verify no other tenants affected in the next hour.

maya-support: Closing for now — reopen if anything else pops up.
